references.context: Commutative algebra: subset S of a commutative unital ring R, containing 1_R and closed under multiplication, used as denominators in ring or module localization.
references.matching_note: Source phrase 'multiplicative subset S' reviewed in context; Both source definitions explicitly use one multiplicatively closed denominator set, containing the unit. A localization construction is not the same meaning as its prerequisite multiplicative subset.

references.disposition: The relation (m,s)∼(m′,s′) when some t∈S annihilates s′m−sm′ is the specific equivalence relation defining this module localization, and the quotient and induced module operations are local to this construction. Multiplicative subsets and ring localization are already separate prerequisites.
The displayed witness is essential to equality of localized module fractions and is not ordinary equality of numerator cross-products.

references.context: Field theory: subfield F of a field E is a subset F⊆E containing 0_E,1_E and closed under inherited field addition, additive inverses, multiplication and inverses of nonzero elements of F, with induced field operations.
references.reason: Subfields are reusable algebraic structures distinct from arbitrary subsets of a field and are needed to identify the image of an injective field homomorphism as an extension.
references.matching_note: Compare with provisional intermediate subfields and generated subfields; this is a general subfield without a designated second base k.

references.disposition: This is the equivalence up to field isomorphism of the two stated extension conventions, not a claim about an arbitrary noninjective ring map.

references.phrase: associated prime p of an R-module M
minimal under inclusion among associated primes
references.context: Order theory: minimal element p of a subset A of a partially ordered set (P,≤), with p∈A and no distinct q∈A satisfying q<p. Here P is the prime ideals ordered by inclusion and A=Ass_R(M); minimality is relative to associated primes rather than all primes.
references.reason: Minimal elements of a partially ordered subset are reusable beyond associated-prime theory and are distinct from minimum/least elements or minimal primes over a chosen ideal.
references.matching_note: Contrast minimum versus minimal and distinguish the relevant subset Ass_R(M) from all prime ideals of R.

references.disposition: The criterion negates minimality inside Ass_R(M), not inside Spec(R) or the annihilator's complete collection of primes.
